measurements.evidence_quote: Zeta potential measurements demonstrated that PET NPs exhibit a negative charge (-20 ± 5 mV), whereas fSPIONs displayed a positive charge (+20 ± 5 mV). || DLS (ZetaPALS, Brookhaven, NY, USA) was used to determine the size of the fSPIONs, PET NPs, and PET–fSPIONs in water. || Samples were allowed to equilibrate in the sample compartment at 25 °C for at least 2 min and measured in acrylic cuvettes (10 × 10 × 45 mm, Sarstedt, Germany) at 25 °C.

The combination of PET NPs with fSPIONs in PET–fSPIONs yielded a composite with a surface charge of +15 ± 4 mV, nearly as positive as that of pure fSPIONs. || DLS (ZetaPALS, Brookhaven, NY, USA) was used to determine the size of the fSPIONs, PET NPs, and PET–fSPIONs in water. || Samples were allowed to equilibrate in the sample compartment at 25 °C for at least 2 min and measured in acrylic cuvettes (10 × 10 × 45 mm, Sarstedt, Germany) at 25 °C. || For analysis of PET–fSPION, the solution was first diluted tenfold with water before the DLS measurement.
